name: staged-empty-partition
origin: real: chrisophus/redline PR #46 (8a53554..a1ae729), the defect verified by reading the code and fixed afterwards
summary: A new 364-line file implementing a fan-out pipeline. Its merge path returns failures[0] to report that every cohort call failed, and reaches that line whenever nothing was kept - including when no cohort was ever drawn, in which case failures is empty and the index panics. Two smaller defects ride with it: the fallback branch drops the cost of the call it already paid for, and a cohort's cross-summary list excludes its peers by name, which nothing makes unique.
why_this_fixture_exists: Every other labelled defect in this set is a wrong answer, a swallowed error or an inverted comparison, so nothing here ever measured whether a review notices code that crashes - and it did not: three runs over this exact diff, two before the reporting rules were changed and one after, produced twenty-three findings about pricing arithmetic and doc comments and none about the index. The crash class was added to the prompt's what-is-worth-reporting list at the same time as this fixture, and this is what says whether that worked.

expect.what: fanOut returns failures[0] when no cohort answered, but reaches that line whenever len(kept) == 0 - including when cohorts itself is empty, which repairPartition returns for a change whose shown set is empty. No call is made, so failures is empty too, and the index panics instead of returning the error.

runStaged's stage-one failure branch returns runOnce's result directly and never folds in the usage stage one was billed for, so a run that paid for two calls records one call's price and joins the one-shot distribution at the wrong cost.

cohortTail drops the other cohorts by comparing Name, and nothing makes stage one's names unique: two cohorts given the same two-or-three-word name each drop the other from the cross-summary list, so the pair most likely to be related is the pair told nothing about each other.

reject.what: claims dividing the response cap by the drawn cohort count instead of the bound lets the staged run spend past the ceiling the tripwire priced
reject.why: repairPartition never returns more cohorts than the bound, so the divisor is at most the bound; n calls at cohortMaxTokens(n) cost at most bound calls at cohortMaxTokens(bound), and Run compares the summed worst case, so the total can only be lower than priced.

reject.what: claims describedBy zeroing stage one's OutputTokens drops that output's cost from the staged run's ledger row
reject.why: describedBy returns the output count separately and runStaged hands it to applySynopsis, which adds it to SynopsisOutputTokens; recost prices that back into CostUSD.

reject.what: claims cohortsRequest inherits a StageSynopsis reference from synopsisRequest that the staged tool array does not declare
reject.why: synopsisRequest sets only Stage, Tail, InputEstimate and costs, cohortsRequest overwrites Stage with StageCohorts, and runOnce picks the tool from res.stage().

reject.what: claims repairPartition can place a file in two cohorts when it folds cohorts over the bound and also appends missed files
reject.why: every file accepted from any cohort, folded ones included, is marked taken before the fold, and the missed pass only collects paths that are not taken.
